prize_parts.citation: for introducing firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, showing how productivity differences, exporting decisions and reallocation across firms shape the gains from trade

statement.case_for: My configuration has changed from B037 to B044. In round 1 I ranked B037 first and B044 third, and the main thing holding B044 back was attribution: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not on the ballot. Several colleagues (Hjalmarsson, Krusell, Friberg and Teorell) answered that concern in round 1. They propose wording the citation around the theory of selection and the gains from trade, not the empirical exporter regularities. They also treat Redding as an extender of the framework and Eaton-Kortum as a different, Ricardian strand. I find that a principled boundary and not merely a compromise. Melitz (2003) is a single originating model that moved trade analysis from industries to firms, and it brought selection into exporting and within-industry reallocation into a tractable general-equilibrium framework. Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exporting versus foreign direct investment is a separable and natural second contribution. The work is over twenty years old, and its qualitative predictions have been tested in firm-level data across many countries. That is a stronger record of confirmation than I can credit to the collateral-amplification channel in B037, where much of the support is calibrated or indirect, as I said in my own round-1 statement. It is also a distinct advance on the increasing-returns trade theory recognised in 2008, and the 2008 prize does not cover this discovery. This is a reassessment on attribution and maturity. It is not a reaction to the support counts, and the fact that B044 has the most explicit supporters is not evidence of merit.
statement.case_against: The attribution gap is real, not resolved. A two-name award leaves out Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum, whose exporter-premium facts and closely related models are part of the field's origin, and it leaves out Redding's quantitative extensions. Framing the citation around theory acknowledges this but does not remove it. The welfare magnitudes depend on functional-form assumptions (Pareto productivity, CES demand), so the citation should rest on the mechanism and not on the size of the gains. Trade was recognised in 2008, and I treat that as a timing and balance consideration only, not a scientific objection. Compared with B037, B044 is a less unusual single-idea attribution, and I still consider Kiyotaki-Moore the most tightly bounded foundational contribution on the list. My own preference there was not overturned on scientific grounds. It was outweighed by the thinner empirical identification and the unresolved overlap with the 2022 prize, which I have not checked against the 2022 scientific background.

responses.point: Strömberg also ranked B037 first, agreeing on the two-name restriction. He accepts that direct empirical identification of the collateral channel is weaker than the theory, and says that more weight on direct empirical confirmation would favour B038 over B037.
responses.response: I share your conclusion on the identification gap, and in round 1 I called it a real reservation. Having heard no direct evidence beyond calibrated models and the general claim that the mechanism disciplined later work, I now weigh it more heavily. We also agreed that our convergence may reflect a shared macro-finance lens. The question I put to myself was which candidate has both a clean boundary and direct confirmation. On that test I find B044 stronger than B038, because its main predictions have been tested repeatedly and its credit boundary is narrower. I keep B037 as an alternative because the mechanism is foundational. I would not treat our agreement as independent evidence.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B044 first and moved from B025 to B044. She argues that the committee should define the award as the theoretical framework of selection and reallocation, not the whole firm-level trade agenda. She separates the well-confirmed qualitative selection mechanism from the model-dependent welfare magnitudes.
responses.response: This was the answer that most changed my view of B044. My round-1 hesitation was that I could not resolve the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum gap from the supplied evidence. Your framing gives a defensible rule: credit the integrated general-equilibrium model of selection and its main extension, and word the citation around the mechanism. I accept that the boundary is still disputable, and I keep it as an uncertainty. I also accept your point that the mechanism, not the welfare magnitudes, should carry the citation. Your remark that you want to guard against over-weighting familiarity is fair, and I apply the same caution to my own macro background.

responses.point: Krusell moved from B017 to B044, citing a cleaner credit boundary and lower topical overlap. He ranks B037 fourth on the overlap with 2022 and mixed empirical validation of the exact amplification channel, and he accepts the Besley question on B017.
responses.response: I disagreed with you in round 1 that the mixed validation should put B037 below B017. I now see the same weakness as relevant when comparing B037 with B044. A mechanism that has shaped a large literature is a real contribution, but it differs from one whose predictions have been confirmed in firm-level data in many countries. On B017, I have not moved my view that the Persson-Tabellini credit is cleaner than the three-name version. I no longer treat B017 as an alternative, because the Besley question is still open and I have not checked the overlap with 2024. I note that we co-author and share an institute, so my agreement with you should not be read as independent corroboration.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B037 second and prefers B044. He notes that Kiyotaki-Moore plus Melitz-Helpman would name four laureates, above the three-laureate cap, and that Eaton-Kortum is a different Ricardian strand, so it is less of a substitute for the Melitz mechanism than the Bernard-Jensen empirical work.
responses.response: I agree on the structural point: B037 and B044 cannot both be recognised in one configuration, so I have to choose, and all the round-1 preferences are single-part. Your distinction between Eaton-Kortum and Bernard-Jensen helps, because it narrows the real attribution gap to the empirical exporter facts that motivated the theory. I do not think that gap disappears, and I would want the citation and the committee's reasoning to say so. I share your view that Redding's contribution is mostly later quantitative extension and does not warrant a third name. We have a co-authored 2026 IJIO paper, which I disclose again below. It is unrelated to any shortlisted candidate.

responses.point: Boppart ranks B038 first with Autor, Hanson and Katz. He accepts that the strands can be separated, and says that if the committee splits them Dorn should displace Katz. He also says the 2023 prize covered Goldin's work on women's labour-market outcomes, not the wage-structure evidence.
responses.response: I accept your reading of 2023 and I now treat the overlap with Katz's work as adjacency, not duplication. I still do not see a stable boundary for B038. Your own point that Dorn should displace Katz if the strands are split shows that the choice is open. My round-1 proposal of Autor and Hanson was one version, and Krusell's Autor-Dorn-Hanson trio is another. Until the committee decides whether this is one discovery or two, I cannot confidently choose among three laureate sets. That is why B038 remains an alternative, not my preferred part. I do not regard B038 as the weaker contribution on scientific impact.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a citation framed around the theory of selection and gains from trade, given that Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum, and possibly Redding, fall outside a two-name award. I cannot settle that boundary from the supplied evidence.
How much the model-dependence of welfare magnitudes (Pareto, CES) should count against the award compared with the well-confirmed qualitative mechanism.

Whether the Kiyotaki-Moore mechanism is sufficiently distinct from the 2022 prize and from the Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist tradition. I have not checked the 2022 scientific background, and the boundary with Gertler and Gilchrist rests on my own knowledge.
Whether B038 is one discovery or two, and whether the right laureate set is Autor-Hanson-Katz, Autor-Hanson or Autor-Dorn-Hanson.
How much neighbouring prizes (2008, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024) should count. I treat them as a timing or balance consideration only when the earlier citation did not cover the same discovery.
My own change of preference is a judgement on attribution and maturity, and I have not independently verified any citation or impact figure.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure. The supplied profile documents no connection to Melitz, Helpman, Kiyotaki, Moore or the other credited names on B038 and B037. I am an IIES colleague and frequent co-author of Krusell (secretary) and Boppart, and I co-authored a 2026 IJIO paper with Friberg. None of those papers concerns a shortlisted candidate. My main research is in macroeconomics, including dynamic public finance, political economy and climate economics. That is field proximity to B037 and to macro-finance generally, and I do not treat it as evidence of merit. As chair I have disclosed that my round-1 preference for B037 was a minority position, and that my speeches for the Academy do not establish voting preferences. The 2018 Scientific Background cites my 2014 paper with Golosov, Krusell and Tsyvinski, but that work is not a shortlisted candidate. Conflicts are disclosed but not adjudicated, and I do not believe any of these ties requires me to limit participation on B044, B037 or B038.
